planting.note: Plant container-grown divisions in spring in very well-drained, lean soil in full sun; Sunny Seduction arose as a naturally occurring sport of 'Summer Pastels' and is propagated vegetatively rather than from seed.

directions: Plant in lean, sharply drained soil in full sun, since rich or consistently damp ground produces weak, floppy stems and invites crown rot. Sunny Seduction opens an intense lemon yellow and gradually softens to pastel yellow as each flat-topped flower cluster ages, giving a two-toned effect across the plant from June into September above ferny, aromatic gray-green foliage. Its stronger, more heavily branched stems resist the splaying habit of older yarrow strains, so it rarely needs staking even in the airy, wildflower-style plantings where yarrow is often used. Shear back spent flower heads to tidy the plant and encourage further bloom, and divide congested clumps every two to three years in spring to maintain vigor.

common_name: Desert Eve Deep Rose Yarrow (Compact Non-Flopping Rose-Pink Yarrow)

planting.note: Plant divisions or container plants in spring in very well-drained, lean soil in full sun; Desert Eve Deep Rose is among the earliest-flowering members of the compact, non-flopping Desert Eve seed strain.

directions: Plant in very well-drained, lean soil in full sun; Desert Eve Deep Rose bears large, flat-topped umbels of saturated rose-pink florets over finely cut, aromatic gray-green foliage, on a compact, sturdy plant bred to resist the flopping that afflicts older yarrow varieties in heat and humidity. It is one of the earliest Achillea selections to flower each year, opening in mid-spring and continuing into summer with regular deadheading. Like all yarrow it demands lean, sharply drained soil rather than rich or consistently moist ground, which promotes crown rot and weak growth. Divide the clump every two to three years in spring to renew vigor and prevent the center from thinning out.

common_name: Desert Eve Terracotta Yarrow (Compact Non-Flopping Orange Yarrow)

planting.note: Plant divisions or container plants in spring in very well-drained, lean soil in full sun; part of the genetically compact Desert Eve seed strain, bred for an early, sturdy, non-flopping habit.

directions: Plant in very well-drained, lean soil in full sun; Desert Eve Terracotta carries showy, flat-topped flower clusters in a warm burnt-orange to toasted-brown tone with a contrasting yellow eye, a distinctly warmer color than the usual yellow or white run of common yarrow. It flowers earlier in the season than most Achillea on the market and holds a compact, well-branched habit over finely cut, aromatic foliage without staking. As with the rest of the Desert Eve strain, avoid rich or constantly moist soil, which invites crown rot and lanky, weak growth in humid conditions. Divide congested clumps every two to three years in spring to keep the planting vigorous and floriferous.

common_name: New Vintage Rose Yarrow (Compact Non-Fading Rose-Pink Yarrow)

planting.note: Plant container-grown starts in spring in very well-drained, lean to average soil in full sun; New Vintage Rose sends up tall, wiry, well-branched flower stems from a tidy basal foliage mound.

directions: Plant in very well-drained, lean to average soil in full sun; excellent drainage is essential, since heavy or wet ground leads to crown rot. New Vintage Rose is a Darwin Perennials breeding selection bearing flat-topped clusters of rose-pink flowers that hold their color well rather than bleaching out as the season progresses, carried on strong stems well above a narrow clump of ferny, aromatic gray-green foliage. It reblooms continuously from late spring through fall with only occasional deadheading, and its narrow footprint suits it to tight border spots and mixed containers despite its taller flowering height. Divide clumps every two to three years in spring to keep the planting vigorous.

common_name: New Vintage Violet Yarrow (Compact Non-Fading Violet Yarrow)

planting.note: Plant container-grown starts in spring in very well-drained, lean to average soil in full sun; New Vintage Violet forms a narrow basal clump topped by taller, well-branched flower stems.

directions: Plant in very well-drained, lean to average soil in full sun, since rich or consistently wet ground encourages weak, rotting crowns. New Vintage Violet is a Darwin Perennials selection bearing tightly held, flat-topped clusters of true violet-magenta flowers that resist the washed-out fading common in older yarrow cultivars, held well above a compact mound of finely cut, aromatic foliage. It reblooms from late spring into fall, is drought- and salt-tolerant once established, and draws bees and butterflies while largely being left alone by deer. Divide clumps every two to three years in spring to maintain vigor and a tidy, upright habit.

planting.note: Plant divisions or container-grown plants in spring into lean, gritty, well-drained soil; Giant Blue is a larger, more vigorous selection than the common Butterfly Blue strain and benefits from slightly wider spacing.

directions: Plant in full sun in well-drained, lean, slightly alkaline soil — like other pincushion flowers, Giant Blue declines quickly in heavy, waterlogged ground. This selection produces noticeably larger lavender-blue, dome-shaped flower heads than standard Butterfly Blue on taller, wiry, branching stems, giving a bolder presence in the border while keeping the same airy, long-wearing bloom habit. It flowers from late spring through fall, pausing only in the hottest part of summer in warmer zones, and responds well to deadheading or a light shearing after each major flush to push out fresh buds. Bees and butterflies visit the nectar-rich flowers heavily, and the long stems make it a good cut flower as well as a border perennial.

planting.note: Plant divisions or container-grown plants in spring into well-drained, evenly moist soil in full sun; Pink Diamonds is a dwarf, mounding selection distinct from the taller columbaria and caucasica pincushion flowers.

directions: Plant in full sun to light afternoon shade in well-drained soil that is kept evenly moist rather than allowed to dry out completely, unlike the lean, drought-tolerant conditions preferred by columbaria types. Pink Diamonds forms a low, dense mound of green foliage topped from summer into fall by shell-pink, lavender-tinged pincushion flowers on short stems, making it well suited to rock gardens, container plantings, and border fronts rather than cutting beds. Its compact, tidy habit needs little staking or division maintenance compared with larger scabiosa types, though light deadheading extends the bloom season. Butterflies and other pollinators visit the flowers readily throughout the summer.
